edges.description: Diverse upstream genetic mechanisms converge on abnormal brain iron deposition.
Iron dyshomeostasis promotes oxidative stress and other neuronal injury pathways.
Neuronal injury in basal ganglia and related networks drives progressive neurologic decline.

Loss of cerebellar neurons is the structural counterpart of this node on imaging, and is the commonest imaging abnormality in the PLAN series this entry cites rather than a feature of every NBIA subtype.

In infantile PLAN the same neuroaxonal injury presents as loss of already acquired motor milestones, so regression is drawn from the injury node rather than from the adult-pattern progressive-decline node below.

In BPAN the cited review places intellectual disability alongside childhood-onset seizures and developmental delay, so it is drawn from the neuronal-injury node rather than from the progressive-decline node, whose cited sentence is about worsening motor and cognitive function.
Dystonia is the core extrapyramidal expression of the basal-ganglia degeneration this node describes.
The parkinsonian arm of the movement-disorder spectrum this node names.
The hyperkinetic expression of the same extrapyramidal degeneration; the cited review groups dystonia, parkinsonism and chorea together as the movement-disorder signs of NBIA.
Pyramidal-tract involvement accompanying the extrapyramidal degeneration presents as spasticity.
The speech disorders the cited review lists among the manifestations of this progressive decline.
Cognitive decline is the non-motor half of the progressive deterioration this node names.
Ataxic gait is among the most frequent features of the adult PLAN presentation, following cerebellar and brainstem involvement.
The ocular abnormalities the cited review lists alongside the motor and cognitive decline; the review does not resolve them further, so this entry records the clinically relevant endpoint.
